tools.name: Neon
tools.summary: Serverless Postgres whose copy-on-write branches can be created per PR via GitHub Actions or per Vercel preview deployment via the Vercel integrations.
tools.summary_short: Copy-on-write Postgres branches per PR or per Vercel preview

engine.quote: Neon is an open-source serverless Postgres database platform.

method.quote: A branch is a copy-on-write clone of your data.

per_pr_automation.quote: this integration creates an isolated database branch for each preview deployment

cleanup.value: Yes: on Git branch delete (Vercel), Action on PR close, or TTL
cleanup.quote: Create branches with TTL by setting an expiration date

data.value: Parent data by default; schema-only option
data.quote: By default, branches are created with all of the data that existed in the parent branch ... Neon also supports schema-only branching.

hosting.quote: Neon offers project deployment in multiple AWS regions.

license.quote: Neon is an open-source serverless Postgres database platform.

pricing.quote: Paid plans are pay-as-you-go: usage is metered hourly and billed at the end of the month, with no monthly minimum.

caveats: Neon is now offered as part of Databricks; docs refer to the product as 'Lakebase Postgres' (https://neon.com/docs/guides/vercel-overview).
With the Vercel-Managed integration, branch cleanup follows Vercel's deployment retention, which can delay deletion by months (https://neon.com/docs/guides/vercel-overview).

The delete-branch GitHub Action is documented for cleaning up 'ephemeral branches after a pull request is merged or closed'; you wire the PR-close trigger yourself (https://neon.com/docs/guides/branching-github-actions).
Azure regions are deprecated for new projects (https://neon.com/docs/introduction/regions).

tools.name: Supabase Branching
tools.summary: Supabase's GitHub integration creates a separate Supabase instance per Git branch/PR, runs migrations and seed.sql, and deletes preview branches when the PR is merged or closed.
tools.summary_short: Separate Supabase instance per Git branch, with migrations and seed

engine.value: Postgres (full Supabase stack: auth, storage, APIs)
engine.quote: a separate environment with its own Supabase instance and API credentials

method.quote: The migrations in the `migrations` subdirectory of your Supabase directory are automatically run when the branch is created.

per_pr_automation.quote: When a new branch is created in GitHub, a corresponding branch is created in Supabase.

cleanup.value: Yes, preview branches deleted on PR merge/close
cleanup.quote: automatically deleted when a PR is merged or closed

data.value: No prod data by default; seed file; dashboard 'Include data' option
data.quote: By default, new branches do not start with any data or storage objects from your base project.

hosting.value: Managed (Supabase Cloud, Pro plan and up)
hosting.quote: run a separate development environment off your production project

license.value: Open source (Apache-2.0); branching is a platform feature
license.quote: Supabase is a combination of open source tools.
license.note: SPDX Apache-2.0 per GitHub repo metadata.

pricing.value: $0.01344 per branch-hour; Pro plan and up

caveats: Persistent branches are not auto-deleted or paused on PR merge/close (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/deployment/branching).
Branching is not on the Free plan (https://supabase.com/pricing).

tools.name: PlanetScale
tools.summary: Managed MySQL (Vitess) and Postgres with development branches; Vitess branches are schema-only by default (data via Data Branching from backup) and schema changes merge via deploy requests; per-PR branches are scripted with the pscale CLI in GitHub Actions.
tools.summary_short: Schema branches (optionally with data) per PR, scripted with the pscale CLI

method.value: Schema-only branch; data branch restored from backup
method.quote: Development branches provide isolated copies of your production database schema

per_pr_automation.value: DIY: pscale CLI in GitHub Actions (setup-pscale-action)
per_pr_automation.quote: You can use `pscale branch create` to create a branch that matches your GitHub branch name.

cleanup.value: Manual or scripted; deploy request can auto-delete branch
cleanup.quote: `--auto-delete-branch` deletes the PlanetScale branch once the deploy request completes, so CI branches don't accumulate.

data.value: Schema-only by default; Data Branching copies latest backup
data.quote: Creates a database branch with both the **schema and data** from the latest backup of the Base branch

hosting.value: Managed; PlanetScale Managed in your AWS/GCP/Azure
hosting.quote: Run PlanetScale in your own AWS, GCP, or Azure account, operated by our team with your data in your cloud.

license.note: CLI license (Apache-2.0) from GitHub repo metadata; the database service is proprietary (Vitess itself is OSS).

pricing.value: No free tier listed; Postgres from $5/mo; branches billed extra

caveats: PlanetScale Postgres branches do not use deploy requests; 'There's currently no automated way to merge schema changes between PlanetScale Postgres branches' (https://planetscale.com/docs/postgres/branching).

Data-seeded branches can't filter out tables/data (no anonymisation) and branches seeded from production are billed as production branches (https://planetscale.com/docs/vitess/schema-changes/data-branching).
Pricing page lists Postgres PS-5 single-node from $5/month and Vitess PS-10 from $39/month (https://planetscale.com/pricing).

tools.name: Xata
tools.summary: Open-source Postgres platform (Kubernetes/CloudNativePG-based) with copy-on-write branches; a GitHub App or GitHub Action creates a branch per pull request, with optional anonymised production clones.
tools.summary_short: Copy-on-write Postgres branches per PR, with anonymised production clones

engine.quote: Xata runs vanilla PostgreSQL with high-performance storage, isolation, and instant branching built in.

method.quote: Create copy-on-write database branches in seconds without duplicating storage.

per_pr_automation.value: Yes, Xata GitHub App or GitHub Action
per_pr_automation.quote: The Xata GitHub App creates a Xata branch for each pull request

cleanup.value: Yes, GitHub App deletes branch on PR close
cleanup.quote: When the pull request closes, the Xata GitHub App deletes the Xata branch.

data.quote: Data masking and anonymization for PostgreSQL dev and testing environments

hosting.value: Managed cloud, BYOC, or self-hosted OSS

license.quote: Xata - Open-source Postgres platform with CoW branching

pricing.value: OSS free; cloud pay-as-you-go, no per-branch fee

caveats: Xata pivoted from its earlier serverless data platform to a branch-native Postgres platform; the OSS release runs on Kubernetes and the README says it is overkill for a single Postgres instance (https://github.com/xataio/xata).
Some multi-tenant security features are kept closed source (https://github.com/xataio/xata).
The documented GitHub Action workflow does not show a PR-close deletion step; the GitHub App does delete on close (https://xata.io/docs/automations/ga-pr).
Cloud compute from $0.012/hr plus $0.28/GB-month storage; BYOC is quoted (https://xata.io/pricing).

tools.name: DBLab Engine (Postgres.ai)
tools.summary: Open-source engine you run yourself that creates thin, writable copy-on-write clones (ZFS or LVM) of large Postgres databases in seconds, with a CI component for testing migrations against clones.
tools.summary_short: Self-hosted thin clones of large Postgres databases in seconds

engine.quote: cloning of 10 TiB PostgreSQL database takes less than 2 seconds when a single user is using the DBLab Engine instance

method.quote: Thin cloning is possible thanks to copy-on-write capabilities provided by either ZFS filesystem or LVM2

per_pr_automation.value: CI via DB Migration Checker GitHub Action (push-triggered)
per_pr_automation.quote: a DLE component that enables integration with CI/CD tools to automatically test migrations in CI/CD pipelines

cleanup.quote: Automated deletion of clones after a specified number of minutes of inactivity (configurable)

data.quote: Allows setting up dynamic masking rules without actual data changes.

hosting.quote: Works well both on-premises and in clouds.

license.quote: DBLab Engine is distributed under Apache 2.0 license.

caveats: Clones are aimed at dev/test and CI; the documented migration-checker trigger is a push event, not a PR preview lifecycle (https://postgres.ai/docs/database-lab/db-migration-checker).
Primary repo is on GitLab (https://gitlab.com/postgres-ai/database-lab); GitHub is a mirror.

tools.name: Turso
tools.summary: Managed SQLite-compatible (libSQL/Turso) databases where a branch is a separate database created from an existing one or a point-in-time snapshot; per-PR branches are scripted via the Platform API in GitHub Actions.
tools.summary_short: Branch a SQLite-compatible database from an existing one or a point in time

method.value: Full copy as separate database; point-in-time option
method.quote: A branch is a separate database instance that is created from an existing database.

per_pr_automation.value: DIY GitHub Actions example via Platform API
per_pr_automation.quote: Automating branching is useful for creating a new database for each pull request.

cleanup.quote: You will need to manually delete the database branch when you no longer need it.

data.value: Copies source data; no anonymisation documented
data.quote: A branch is a separate database instance that is created from an existing database.

hosting.quote: Fully managed platform for Turso and libSQL databases

license.note: MIT per GitHub repo license metadata; branching is a Turso Cloud feature.

pricing.value: Free plan (100 DBs); branching adds no usage cost
pricing.quote: Point-in-time restore and database branching do not add usage cost.

caveats: Branches count towards the plan's database quota (https://docs.turso.tech/features/branching).
The sample workflow triggers on ref creation, not PR events (https://docs.turso.tech/features/branching).

tools.name: Prisma Postgres
tools.feature_name: Preview databases (GitHub Actions) / Compute branch previews
tools.summary: Managed Postgres without data branching; previews get a fresh database per PR (GitHub Actions guide) or per Git branch on Prisma Compute, with migrations and seed data applied.
tools.summary_short: Fresh, migrated and seeded Postgres database per PR

engine.quote: Prisma Postgres is managed PostgreSQL 17 with PgBouncer pooling on every plan

method.value: New empty database per PR, migrated and seeded
method.quote: applies your checked-in migrations, seeds it with sample data

per_pr_automation.value: GitHub Actions guide; Prisma Compute branch previews
per_pr_automation.quote: The workflow provisions a database for every pull request

cleanup.value: Yes, on PR close (workflow) or Git branch delete (Compute)
cleanup.quote: When the pull request is closed, the workflow deletes the database.

data.value: Seeded only; production data not copied
data.quote: its own new database; production data is not copied

hosting.quote: Prisma Postgres is managed PostgreSQL 17 with PgBouncer pooling on every plan

license.note: Closed-source commercial service; no open-source license is published (inferred).

pricing.value: Free: 50 DBs, 2 GB; paid billed per operation

caveats: No copy-on-write/data branching; each preview starts from a new database (https://www.prisma.io/docs/compute/branching).
Compute per-branch databases apply only to databases declared in the Prisma Composer (Early Access) module (https://www.prisma.io/docs/compute/branching).

tools.name: Tonic Structural
tools.summary: Commercial test-data platform that de-identifies, masks and subsets production data from many databases into realistic datasets for staging/dev; it feeds preview databases rather than provisioning them per PR.
tools.summary_short: De-identifies and subsets production data for non-production databases

engine.value: Postgres, MySQL, SQL Server, Oracle, MongoDB, more
engine.quote: native connectors to all the leading relational and NoSQL databases, data warehouses, lakehouses, and file types.

method.quote: The Tonic Structural platform creates safe, realistic datasets to use in staging environments or for local development.

per_pr_automation.note: No documented per-PR integration; vendor mentions CI/CD pipeline integration generally.

cleanup.note: Not documented; Structural writes datasets, does not manage preview DB lifecycle.

data.quote: Automatically detect PII and PHI throughout your data

hosting.quote: Deploy a self-hosted instance of Structural, or work with your data in our Cloud offering.

license.note: Closed-source commercial service; no open-source license is published (inferred).

pricing.value: Custom annual pricing by source-data volume
pricing.quote: Annual pricing for Tonic Structural is determined by the Plan you select and the amount of source data connected to Tonic.

caveats: Tonic Ephemeral (its on-demand ephemeral database product) is no longer in Tonic's docs and its product URL redirects to the homepage; see excluded.
No free tier listed for Structural (https://www.tonic.ai/pricing).

excluded.name: Tonic Ephemeral
excluded.reason: No longer present in Tonic docs (docs.tonic.ai/ephemeral 404, not in sitemap) and product URL redirects to homepage; appears discontinued (not confirmed by an announcement).

excluded.name: MongoDB Atlas
excluded.reason: No documented database branching / per-PR preview feature found; skipped per scope.
